title: React Interview Questions Core Check
description: Check your understanding of React interview fundamentals, hooks, performance, coding challenges, and frontend system design answers.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: In an interview, how should you explain what problem React solves?

options.text: It helps build UI from reusable components that update predictably with state

questions.explanation: Core React answers should connect components, state, and declarative rendering.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between props and state?

options.text: Props are passed in; state is owned and updated by a component or hook
Props can change but state never changes
State only works in class components

questions.explanation: Props are inputs from parents; state is local owned data that can trigger re-renders.

questions.prompt: Which are Rules of Hooks? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Call Hooks at the top level
Call Hooks only from React functions or custom Hooks
Call Hooks inside loops when convenient
Call Hooks conditionally after early returns

questions.explanation: Hooks rely on consistent call order, so they belong at the top level of React functions or custom hooks.

questions.prompt: What is a stale closure in a hook-related interview answer?

options.text: A callback or effect reading an older captured value than expected
A CSS class that is unused
A source map from an old build

questions.explanation: Stale closures happen when functions capture values from a previous render.

options.text: Storing mutable values or DOM references that should not trigger re-renders

questions.explanation: Refs persist across renders without causing re-renders when changed.

questions.prompt: What should you do before applying React.memo in a performance interview scenario?

options.text: Identify whether re-renders are the real bottleneck

questions.explanation: Strong performance answers begin with measurement and bottleneck identification.

options.text: Rendering too many visible and offscreen list items at once

questions.explanation: Virtualization limits rendered rows to the visible window plus a buffer.

questions.prompt: What makes a good frontend system design answer?

options.text: Requirements, data flow, component boundaries, performance, failures, and tradeoffs

questions.explanation: System design interviews evaluate structured reasoning and tradeoffs, not only tool selection.
